key_insight: A multiplier-free compensated tangential velocity ALE-FEM redistributes boundary nodes in a way that preserves energy stability for Navier–Stokes free-boundary flows.
engineering_relevance: The scheme provides a robust, well-posed, energy-dissipative tool for simulating surface-tension-driven interfaces while improving mesh quality, especially for challenging viscosity–surface-tension regimes.
method: Energy-stable ALE finite element formulation for incompressible Navier–Stokes free boundaries
Compensated tangential velocity driven by discrete tangential curvature residual
Relaxation parameter scaled by viscous-capillary balance: alpha = gamma0 / mu
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical proof of well-posedness, energy dissipation, and temporal consistency, plus numerical tests showing robustness across multiple mu and gamma0 values and better mesh quality than BGN.
watch_item: Performance may depend on choosing the relaxation scaling and time step appropriately, particularly in the small-time-step regime where mesh behavior is most sensitive.
paper_title: An energy--stable ALE--FEM with compensated tangential velocity for Navier--Stokes free--boundary flows
